Text: AI stocks rebounded Monday, but debt risks remain a major concern. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1%. Oracle ($ORCL) rose 1%, Intel ($INTC) gained 2.4%, AMD ($AMD) climbed 1.8% and Micron Technology ($MU) added 3%. CoreWeave ($CRWV) closed fractionally lower after hitting a 52-week low. The bond market tells a more troubling story. CoreWeave’s 9.625% bond due in 2032 yielded 14.9%, while its five-year credit default swap spread stood near 1,082 basis points—a distressed level signaling serious credit concerns. Oracle faces scrutiny, too. S&P rates it BBB-, the lowest investment-grade rating; Fitch rates it BBB and Moody’s Baa2. Oracle’s five-year credit default swap spread reached 315 basis points Monday, up 311% year over year, according to CNBC. The takeaway: AI demand is strong, but financing its infrastructure carries growing risks. Watch debt costs, refinancing needs and cash flow. A downgrade of Oracle to junk status could signal broader credit contagion across the AI trade. (CNBC)
